card.summary: A blue‑sided, single‑story colonial bungalow with four rooms, a front porch, and a rear yard swing.
card.description: The residence is a single‑story colonial bungalow measuring 792 cm wide by 1417 cm deep, finished in a vibrant blue vinyl siding that catches the eye from the front gate. A modest 259 cm high ceiling runs throughout the four‑room layout, providing generous vertical space while preserving the intimate scale of a 1920s pattern‑book home. The front porch, 300 cm by 400 cm, is clad in pressure‑treated decking and edged with a sleek metal railing, inviting a warm welcome. Inside, hard‑wood interior doors and aluminum‑frame sliding windows punctuate the walls, while the kitchen boasts custom hardwood cabinets and a period‑appropriate model kitchen layout. The bathroom features classic ceramic fixtures and a claw‑foot tub, echoing the era’s charm. A blue‑painted front door with a brass hinge opens onto a concrete slab foundation, and the roof is supported by timber trusses sheathed in asphalt shingles. In the rear yard, a galvanized steel swing set anchored 300 cm from the fence offers a playful focal point, its seat and flexible chains designed for safe, rhythmic motion. All elements are coordinated to meet modern building codes while preserving the nostalgic aesthetic of a 1920s colonial bungalow.

Draft a site plan showing the blue exterior finish, a front porch, and a swing set positioned 300 cm from the rear fence.
Obtain permits for foundation, framing, electrical, plumbing, and the yard swing structure.
Excavate and pour a 15 cm thick concrete slab foundation with integrated footings.
Erect wood framing, install sheathing, roof trusses, and apply blue vinyl siding with matching trim.
Finish interior walls, install doors, windows, fixtures, and complete the swing set anchoring before final inspection.

Ceiling height is taken as 259 cm per the reference designs, providing a comfortable 2.59 m interior volume.
A single‑car garage is omitted, as the brief mentions only a swing in the yard and no garage requirement.
Standard modern mechanical systems (HVAC, electrical panel, plumbing) are assumed to meet current code while remaining invisible to the historic façade.

card.summary: A single‑story blue clapboard home with porch, three bedrooms, a bathroom suite, and a rear‑yard swing set, built to 1920s bungalow proportions and modern BIM standards.
card.description: The blue‑clad residence stands proudly on a 792 cm × 1416 cm concrete slab, its wood clapboard walls painted a crisp azure that catches the sun on every side. A modest gabled roof of asphalt shingles crowns the single‑story, 300 cm‑high volume, while a welcoming front porch of 300 cm × 600 cm concrete extends the living space outward, shaded by a shallow overhang that mirrors the roof’s pitch. The façade is punctuated by eight double‑hung windows, each sliding on a smooth track, and a solid oak front door with a brass hinge, inviting guests into a layout of three bedrooms, a central living room, and a compact yet efficient bathroom. Inside the bathroom, an acrylic bathtub bubbles with warm water, a ceramic low‑profile toilet sits flush against the wall, and a porcelain sink rests beside it, all serviced by concealed plumbing that runs beneath the subfloor. Beyond the house, a steel swing set with a wooden seat is anchored in the rear yard, framed by a simple wooden fence and a hinged front gate that frames the entryway. Every component—from the 30 cm‑thick timber joists to the 5 cm‑wide roof trusses—has been dimensioned to fit precisely within the overall envelope, delivering a harmonious blend of classic colonial massing and playful modern amenities.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions and mark the footprint of the 792 cm × 1416 cm blue house.
Draft a site plan showing the house, front porch, swing set location, and utility routes.
Excavate and pour a reinforced concrete foundation slab to the exact footprint.
Erect timber floor joists, sheathe the subfloor, and frame the exterior walls with 30 cm‑thick clapboard studs.
Install roof trusses, sheathing, and finish with asphalt shingles while adding dormer details for visual interest.
Finish interior finishes, install bathroom fixtures, attach the swing set, and conduct a final inspection.
assumptions: The house adopts the 1‑story, 4‑room (3 bedrooms + living) layout of the Desoto pattern, as the brief does not specify room count.
Roof pitch is assumed to be 30°, typical of shingled colonial bungalows, to match the reference designs.
A standard 3‑meter ceiling height is used for all interior spaces, giving a total building height of approximately 300 cm.
The swing set is placed 300 cm from the rear wall to allow safe clearance, a common yard layout for suburban homes.
questions: Do you prefer a single‑panel or double‑panel front door, and should it include sidelights?
What finish material and color would you like for the interior walls and flooring beyond the blue exterior?
Will the bathtub be a freestanding soaking tub or a built‑in alcove unit, and do you require a separate shower enclosure?
